statements.flow-rate-velocity: The flow rate is the cross-sectional area of the conduit times the average velocity of the fluid across it, $Q = A\bar{v}$. Flow rate and velocity are therefore related but different quantities: a wide, slow river can carry more water than a narrow, fast one.
statements.pressure-drops-in-fast-fluid: Where a fluid speeds up, its pressure drops. A fluid flowing into a narrower channel gains kinetic energy, and that energy comes from the net work done by the higher pressure behind it pushing it into the channel.
statements.flow-resistance: The resistance to flow is defined by the relationship between flow rate and pressure difference: the flow rate is the pressure difference divided by the resistance, $Q = (P_2 - P_1)/R$, and it is in the direction from high to low pressure. The resistance includes everything except pressure that affects the flow rate.
statements.reynolds-number: The Reynolds number for flow in a tube, $N_{\text{R}} = 2\rho vr/\eta$, is a dimensionless quantity that reveals whether the flow is likely to be laminar or turbulent.
statements.reynolds-number-object: The Reynolds number for an object moving in a fluid, ${N'}_{\text{R}} = \rho vL/\eta$, where $L$ is a characteristic length of the object, indicates whether the flow around it is laminar or turbulent. A moving object in a still fluid is equivalent to a stationary object in a flowing stream.
statements.torricellis-theorem: Fluid leaving a reservoir through an opening a height $h$ below its surface emerges at the speed it would have if it had fallen freely through that height, $v_2^2 = v_1^2 + 2gh$, whatever the size of the opening.
statements.random-walk-distance: The root-mean-square distance a molecule travels by diffusion is proportional to the square root of the time, $x_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{2Dt}$, not to the time itself, which is what makes diffusion so slow over any large distance.
statements.semipermeable-membrane: A semipermeable membrane allows only certain small molecules to pass through it. Membranes in living things are generally of this kind, and they affect the rates at which substances diffuse across them.

new.name: Fluid dynamics
new.statement: Fluid dynamics is the physics of fluids in motion.

new.name: The liter, $1\;\text{L} = 10^{-3}\;\text{m}^3$
new.statement: A liter is a unit of volume equal to $10^{-3}\;\text{m}^3$, or 1000 cubic centimeters.

new.name: Relative osmotic pressure
new.statement: Relative osmotic pressure is the back pressure that stops the osmotic process when neither solution is pure water.

new.name: Reverse osmosis
new.statement: Reverse osmosis is the process that occurs when back pressure is great enough to reverse the normal direction of osmosis, driving water out of the more concentrated solution. It is used to desalinate water by forcing it through a membrane that will not pass salt.

new.name: Reverse dialysis
new.statement: Reverse dialysis is the process that occurs when back pressure is great enough to reverse the normal direction of dialysis, and it can be used to filter out a substance that a membrane will not pass.
